mission.title: fluent-bit: Watch TLS certificates and reload on changes
mission.description: Watch TLS certificates and reload on changes. Requested by 10+ users.

steps.title: Check current fluent-bit deployment
steps.description:
Verify your fluent-bit version and configuration:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n fluent-bit -l app.kubernetes.io/name=fluent-bit
helm list -n fluent-bit 2>/dev/null || echo "Not installed via Helm"
```
This feature requires a working fluent-bit installation.

steps.title: Review fluent-bit configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant fluent-bit configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n fluent-bit -l app.kubernetes.io/name=fluent-bit
kubectl get configmap -n fluent-bit -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=fluent-bit
```
See #9718 and #1678
Short lived client certificates are the norm. fluent-bit does not reload TLS certificates when they are renewed and simply fails at shipping logs.

steps.title: Apply the fix for Watch TLS certificates and reload on changes
steps.description:
On the current shorter validness of certificates proposals, we need to handle reloading certificates on Linux.
This is because shorter period of certificates" validness requests us to relaunching Fluent Bit executable before reaching the expire date of the certificates.

steps.title: Verify the feature works
steps.description:
Test that the new capability is working as expected:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n fluent-bit -l app.kubernetes.io/name=fluent-bit
kubectl get events -n fluent-bit --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm the feature described in "Watch TLS certificates and reload on changes" is functioning correctly.

resolution.summary:
On the current shorter validness of certificates proposals, we need to handle reloading certificates on Linux.
This is because shorter period of certificates" validness requests us to relaunching Fluent Bit executable before reaching the expire date of the certificates.

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with fluent-bit installed or the issue environment reproducible.
